stem: In children older than 18 months, why is an open reduction alone often insufficient for treating a dislocated hip?

options.text: The femoral head has become too large to fit in the socket.
They lack sufficient remodeling potential for the acetabulum to grow back to normal.
Bracing with a Pavlik harness is more effective at this age.
Closed reduction is always successful in this age group.

explanation: By this age, the natural ability of the hip socket to reshape itself is diminished, requiring surgical intervention (osteotomy) to reshape it.
rationale: Consider the biological limits of bone growth and self-correction as a child ages.

optionExplanations.A: While size can be an issue, the primary reason provided is the lack of natural growth potential to fix the socket's shape.
optionExplanations.B: By this age, the natural ability of the hip socket to reshape itself is diminished, requiring surgical intervention (osteotomy) to reshape it.
optionExplanations.C: A Pavlik harness is typically used for infants under 6 months; it is generally not used for older children needing surgery.
optionExplanations.D: Closed reduction is actually less likely to succeed as the child gets older, often necessitating open surgery.

source.hint: Consider the biological limits of bone growth and self-correction as a child ages.
